Coding orchestrators & multi-agent syste: *Drive several coding agents — in parallel (fleets in isolated git worktrees) or in a disciplined pipeline with adversarial review.*
Codebase knowledge: graphs, search & mem: *Give the agent a structured understanding of the project (and its history), reducing the context to load.*
Token & agent-behavior optimization: *Reduce what the agent consumes (input) or produces (output / code scope).*
Workflow, methodology & spec-driven deve: *Structure the AI-assisted dev process (methodologies, roles, specs, guided workflows) on top of an existing agent.*
Browser automation (MCP servers): *Drive a browser from the agent — mainly to **test** the web apps being built (and scraping/control). LLM cost on the client side → 🟢.*
AI assistants for terminal / shell: *Conversational AI companions integrated into the terminal: command execution (with safeguards), system analysis, CLI help.*
AI code review:
*AI reviewers that read PRs (summary, bugs, security) — the key lever when agents produce more code than is being reviewed. The LLM is **included in the price** (📦), not BYOK. Conceptual framing: [📄 agentic code review](../concepts/agentic-code-review.md).*
> **Key takeaway**: low overlap between tools (~93% of findings are seen by only one of the 4) → combine several with complementary strengths (precision vs recall); treat their verdicts as **signals**, the human keeps the merge.
Documentation & external knowledge sourc: *Serve the agent **up-to-date external knowledge** — library docs, GitHub repos, vendor docs (Microsoft/AWS), web — to produce correct code without hallucinating signatures. They run inside the agent (LLM cost on the client side → 🟢) and aim to *reduce* tokens. ⚠️ Exception: **Exa** relies on a **pay-per-use** search API (cost separate from the LLM).*
CI/CD, delivery & AI-assisted operations:
*The **right-hand end** of the SDLC: **shipping** code (CI/merge/flaky tests) and **operating** prod (**AI SRE**: incident investigation, RCA, self-healing). ⚠️ The ops side spills over into "operating a product" (boundary with *embedding AI into a product*). LLM run by the vendor (SaaS) → **📦 included**; AI SREs are mostly **enterprise / quote-based**.*
> **Unverified candidates** (to be arbitrated, cf. `tool-candidates.md`): **Datadog Bits AI Dev Agent** (autonomous flaky fix → draft PR), **Aviator**, **Trunk** (CI/flaky); **Rootly**, **PagerDuty AIOps** (incident/AIOps).
RAG infrastructure / vector databases:
*Technical building blocks on which search/RAG applications are built.*
> **LLM-cost reading key**: a vector database **stores and searches vectors** that you provide (BYO embeddings) → it does not call an LLM, hence **🟢** across the board. Several offer **optional** hosted embedding generation (billed per token) or via your provider key (BYOK) — detailed in each note. Structuring choice: **stay in Postgres** (pgvector), **embedded** (Chroma, LanceDB), **open-source server** (Qdrant, Weaviate, Milvus) or **managed proprietary** (Pinecone, turbopuffer).
General-purpose multi-agent frameworks (:
*Libraries to build your own multi-agent systems — general-purpose, not coding-specific.*
> **Reading key**: these frameworks **orchestrate** model calls → all **🔑 BYOK** (you provide your keys; they don't bill tokens, except an optional gateway). The choice axis: **low-level/control** (LangGraph), **conversational** (AutoGen/AG2), **minimalist** (OpenAI Agents SDK), **roles** (CrewAI), **data/RAG** (LlamaIndex), **type-safe** (Pydantic AI), **TypeScript** (Mastra). Several have a **concept note** in `concepts/` (theory) in addition to the tool note (product/price).
Specialized knowledge & data sources (MC: *MCP servers exposing authoritative data/knowledge corpora to agents (regulations, reference frameworks…), without LLM generation.*
Multi-agent orchestration & enterprise a: *Platforms that coordinate AI agents within business processes (beyond coding).*
Domain-specialized autonomous agents: *AI agents dedicated to a specific business domain (here: offensive security / pentest), beyond general-purpose coding.*
Security — tools exposed via MCP: *🔐 Security tools drivable by the agent: **offensive** (Kali, Burp, ZAP — authorized testing only, isolated environment) and **defensive** (Snyk — vulnerability scanning of your own code).*
Computer / desktop control: *Give the model the ability to **act** directly on an environment. **computer use** is an exception among MCP servers: it is the model itself that acts, billed in API tokens → 💸.*
LLMOps — evaluation & observability:
*Control an LLM's behavior **in production**: **trace** each run (debug a request), **evaluate** quality (datasets, LLM-as-judge, CI), **observe** cost, latency and errors over time. Cross-cutting building blocks of an AI app's lifecycle — not coding assistance.*
> **Special case of LLM cost**: these tools **observe your own calls** without calling an LLM themselves → 🟢 for tracing/observability. But **LLM-as-judge evaluation** consumes tokens → 🔑 BYOK (sometimes resold per use). Hence the dual icon 🟢🔑. Helicone (a pure observability proxy) can even *reduce* your LLM bill via its cache.
LLM gateways / routers:
*A **single API** (OpenAI-compatible) in front of dozens of providers: route by price/perf, switch to a **fallback** if a provider goes down, pool keys, budgets and observability. A building block directly tied to **cost control** and to a product's multi-provider resilience. Background concept: [LLM observability — best practices](../concepts/llm-observability-best-practices.md).*
> **LLM-cost reading key**: two models stand opposed. **Self-host / pass-through** gateways ([LiteLLM](../tools/litellm.md), [Portkey](../tools/portkey.md)) do **not** bill tokens — you keep your direct relationship with the provider (🔑 BYOK). **Hosted** gateways ([OpenRouter](../tools/openrouter.md), [Requesty](../tools/requesty.md)) may **resell inference** with fees/margin (💸), while often offering a BYOK mode (🔑).
Coding agents & IDEs: *Do the coding work — or orchestrate the agents that do it.*
Shared agent learning & knowledge common: *Cross-agent knowledge commons: agents persist, share and query learnings (pitfalls, fixes) so they stop rediscovering the same failures in isolation. Open standards over per-vendor lock-in.*
